title: Formalizing all indexed mathematics as a benchmark for general reasoning, with the example of implementing dilatations of categories
summary: Formal rigor distinguishes mathematics from other disciplines, in the sense that mathematical statements are derived from explicit axioms by logically verifiable steps. Interactive theorem provers support this by expressing definitions, theorems, and proofs in a fully formal language and verifying them mechanically. We consider the benchmark problem of formalizing all published mathematics as a machine verifiable and continuously updated corpus of mathematical knowledge.
